# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1504
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1504
- **Title**: perf(1497): incremental TrajectorySnapshotBuilder publishing — O(delta) per append
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1497-trajectory-append-o-n` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +595
- **Deletions**: -96
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:08:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T17:16:29Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1497

## Hot path (confirmed)

Every `append()`/`applyEvent()` materialized a snapshot by copying every ledger row (`List.of`), rebuilding the whole `recordLocations` map, and re-sorting + re-folding cumulative usage over **every** request fact — O(n) per append, O(n²) per live session. Bulk `appendAll` was already linear; the live tail was the slide-show.

**Before/after (4 records/turn synthetic, warmed VM, standalone Dart SDK 3.13.5):**

| shape | before (main @ 0c602bf47e) | after |
|---|---|---|
| live tail, 65k `append()` = 65k snapshots | **380 895 ms (~6.3 min)** | **92 ms (~4 100×)** |
| per-append cost, 1k → 80k records | 60 µs → ~5-10 ms (grows linearly with n) | flat **~1.5-2.3 µs** |
| bulk `appendAll` 65k | ~100 ms (already linear) | ~98 ms (unchanged) |

## Fix (algorithmic, per the card)

- **Chunked row store with copy-on-write publishing**: 512-row chunks; a snapshot publishes an immutable chunk-pointer list (O(chunks) refs); the next cycle clones a chunk before its first in-place write. Published snapshots stay byte-identical and immutable.
- **Lazy `recordLocations`**: derived on first access per snapshot (no lib/ reader touches it on the append path; identical content to the eager map).
- **Incremental requests cache**: cached sorted-fact order + built numbers + running cumulative usage; a snapshot rebuilds only the suffix at/after the first touched fact. New facts always fold in at the sorted tail (order = row count at creation, which only grows); anything the incremental path cannot prove order-stable falls back to the **exact full sort** the old code ran.
- **Streamed-row replacement** truncates a contiguous tail and drops only the cut tool-row indexes; non-tail placement keeps the legacy filter + full rebuild.

## Regression guards (bounded, not flake-prone)

- `snapshotRowCopies` counter (the `chainWalkHops` pattern, deterministic): measured **150 rows/append**, envelope 600/append — the quadratic shape copies ~n/2 rows per append and fails it by 3 orders of magnitude. No wall-clock ratio asserted: the #358 flake lesson, plus a measured 60× JIT-tier cliff on cold first runs.
- Absolute 8 s budget on a 20k live-tail run (fixed: <100 ms warm, ~2.1 s worst cold; pre-fix measured 31 s) — well under the 30 s per-test timeout cap.
- 50k `appendAll` open-budget check (issue acceptance), snapshot-immutability-under-later-appends (chunk sharing + lazy locations freeze), bulk-replay request folding (facts created + finalized between snapshots).

## Gates

- `dart analyze`: 0 issues on changed files (repo-wide 132 pre-existing infos, identical with the change stashed).
- `dart test test/trajectory/` 200 ✓ + event-handler/compaction 31 ✓ + `test/integration/trajectory/snapshot_builder_integration_test.dart` 6 ✓ (live-vs-replay requests compared field-by-field).
- `dart format` clean.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: all three card items — profile bench (1k/10k/50k/65k synthetic, growth asserted), per-append copying eliminated (structural sharing + invalidatable derived cache; `_snapshot` now O(delta)), snapshots cheap (shared refs + suffix fold; 546 ms instrumented mean → µs).
Remaining (not in scope here): the fold path itself shows a cold-run JIT-tier cliff (~100 µs/append unwarmed, ~1.7 µs warmed — same code pre/post, deterministic counters unaffected); a follow-up could warm or restructure `_appendRecord` if cold-start latency ever matters.

  dmtools <tool> --file params.json     # Execute with JSON file

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1504
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1504
- **Title**: perf(1497): incremental TrajectorySnapshotBuilder publishing — O(delta) per append
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1497-trajectory-append-o-n` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +595
- **Deletions**: -96
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:08:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T17:16:29Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1497

## Hot path (confirmed)

Every `append()`/`applyEvent()` materialized a snapshot by copying every ledger row (`List.of`), rebuilding the whole `recordLocations` map, and re-sorting + re-folding cumulative usage over **every** request fact — O(n) per append, O(n²) per live session. Bulk `appendAll` was already linear; the live tail was the slide-show.

**Before/after (4 records/turn synthetic, warmed VM, standalone Dart SDK 3.13.5):**

| shape | before (main @ 0c602bf47e) | after |
|---|---|---|
| live tail, 65k `append()` = 65k snapshots | **380 895 ms (~6.3 min)** | **92 ms (~4 100×)** |
| per-append cost, 1k → 80k records | 60 µs → ~5-10 ms (grows linearly with n) | flat **~1.5-2.3 µs** |
| bulk `appendAll` 65k | ~100 ms (already linear) | ~98 ms (unchanged) |

## Fix (algorithmic, per the card)

- **Chunked row store with copy-on-write publishing**: 512-row chunks; a snapshot publishes an immutable chunk-pointer list (O(chunks) refs); the next cycle clones a chunk before its first in-place write. Published snapshots stay byte-identical and immutable.
- **Lazy `recordLocations`**: derived on first access per snapshot (no lib/ reader touches it on the append path; identical content to the eager map).
- **Incremental requests cache**: cached sorted-fact order + built numbers + running cumulative usage; a snapshot rebuilds only the suffix at/after the first touched fact. New facts always fold in at the sorted tail (order = row count at creation, which only grows); anything the incremental path cannot prove order-stable falls back to the **exact full sort** the old code ran.
- **Streamed-row replacement** truncates a contiguous tail and drops only the cut tool-row indexes; non-tail placement keeps the legacy filter + full rebuild.

## Regression guards (bounded, not flake-prone)

- `snapshotRowCopies` counter (the `chainWalkHops` pattern, deterministic): measured **150 rows/append**, envelope 600/append — the quadratic shape copies ~n/2 rows per append and fails it by 3 orders of magnitude. No wall-clock ratio asserted: the #358 flake lesson, plus a measured 60× JIT-tier cliff on cold first runs.
- Absolute 8 s budget on a 20k live-tail run (fixed: <100 ms warm, ~2.1 s worst cold; pre-fix measured 31 s) — well under the 30 s per-test timeout cap.
- 50k `appendAll` open-budget check (issue acceptance), snapshot-immutability-under-later-appends (chunk sharing + lazy locations freeze), bulk-replay request folding (facts created + finalized between snapshots).

## Gates

- `dart analyze`: 0 issues on changed files (repo-wide 132 pre-existing infos, identical with the change stashed).
- `dart test test/trajectory/` 200 ✓ + event-handler/compaction 31 ✓ + `test/integration/trajectory/snapshot_builder_integration_test.dart` 6 ✓ (live-vs-replay requests compared field-by-field).
- `dart format` clean.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: all three card items — profile bench (1k/10k/50k/65k synthetic, growth asserted), per-append copying eliminated (structural sharing + invalidatable derived cache; `_snapshot` now O(delta)), snapshots cheap (shared refs + suffix fold; 546 ms instrumented mean → µs).
Remaining (not in scope here): the fold path itself shows a cold-run JIT-tier cliff (~100 µs/append unwarmed, ~1.7 µs warmed — same code pre/post, deterministic counters unaffected); a follow-up could warm or restructure `_appendRecord` if cold-start latency ever matters.

# pr-1504: perf(1497): incremental TrajectorySnapshotBuilder publishing — O(delta) per append

## Description

Fixes #1497

## Hot path (confirmed)

Every `append()`/`applyEvent()` materialized a snapshot by copying every ledger row (`List.of`), rebuilding the whole `recordLocations` map, and re-sorting + re-folding cumulative usage over **every** request fact — O(n) per append, O(n²) per live session. Bulk `appendAll` was already linear; the live tail was the slide-show.

**Before/after (4 records/turn synthetic, warmed VM, standalone Dart SDK 3.13.5):**

| shape | before (main @ 0c602bf47e) | after |
|---|---|---|
| live tail, 65k `append()` = 65k snapshots | **380 895 ms (~6.3 min)** | **92 ms (~4 100×)** |
| per-append cost, 1k → 80k records | 60 µs → ~5-10 ms (grows linearly with n) | flat **~1.5-2.3 µs** |
| bulk `appendAll` 65k | ~100 ms (already linear) | ~98 ms (unchanged) |

## Fix (algorithmic, per the card)

- **Chunked row store with copy-on-write publishing**: 512-row chunks; a snapshot publishes an immutable chunk-pointer list (O(chunks) refs); the next cycle clones a chunk before its first in-place write. Published snapshots stay byte-identical and immutable.
- **Lazy `recordLocations`**: derived on first access per snapshot (no lib/ reader touches it on the append path; identical content to the eager map).
- **Incremental requests cache**: cached sorted-fact order + built numbers + running cumulative usage; a snapshot rebuilds only the suffix at/after the first touched fact. New facts always fold in at the sorted tail (order = row count at creation, which only grows); anything the incremental path cannot prove order-stable falls back to the **exact full sort** the old code ran.
- **Streamed-row replacement** truncates a contiguous tail and drops only the cut tool-row indexes; non-tail placement keeps the legacy filter + full rebuild.

## Regression guards (bounded, not flake-prone)

- `snapshotRowCopies` counter (the `chainWalkHops` pattern, deterministic): measured **150 rows/append**, envelope 600/append — the quadratic shape copies ~n/2 rows per append and fails it by 3 orders of magnitude. No wall-clock ratio asserted: the #358 flake lesson, plus a measured 60× JIT-tier cliff on cold first runs.
- Absolute 8 s budget on a 20k live-tail run (fixed: <100 ms warm, ~2.1 s worst cold; pre-fix measured 31 s) — well under the 30 s per-test timeout cap.
- 50k `appendAll` open-budget check (issue acceptance), snapshot-immutability-under-later-appends (chunk sharing + lazy locations freeze), bulk-replay request folding (facts created + finalized between snapshots).

## Gates

- `dart analyze`: 0 issues on changed files (repo-wide 132 pre-existing infos, identical with the change stashed).
- `dart test test/trajectory/` 200 ✓ + event-handler/compaction 31 ✓ + `test/integration/trajectory/snapshot_builder_integration_test.dart` 6 ✓ (live-vs-replay requests compared field-by-field).
- `dart format` clean.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: all three card items — profile bench (1k/10k/50k/65k synthetic, growth asserted), per-append copying eliminated (structural sharing + invalidatable derived cache; `_snapshot` now O(delta)), snapshots cheap (shared refs + suffix fold; 546 ms instrumented mean → µs).
Remaining (not in scope here): the fold path itself shows a cold-run JIT-tier cliff (~100 µs/append unwarmed, ~1.7 µs warmed — same code pre/post, deterministic counters unaffected); a follow-up could warm or restructure `_appendRecord` if cold-start latency ever matters.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1504
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1504
- **Title**: perf(1497): incremental TrajectorySnapshotBuilder publishing — O(delta) per append
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1497-trajectory-append-o-n` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +595
- **Deletions**: -96
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:08:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T17:16:29Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1497

## Hot path (confirmed)

Every `append()`/`applyEvent()` materialized a snapshot by copying every ledger row (`List.of`), rebuilding the whole `recordLocations` map, and re-sorting + re-folding cumulative usage over **every** request fact — O(n) per append, O(n²) per live session. Bulk `appendAll` was already linear; the live tail was the slide-show.

**Before/after (4 records/turn synthetic, warmed VM, standalone Dart SDK 3.13.5):**

| shape | before (main @ 0c602bf47e) | after |
|---|---|---|
| live tail, 65k `append()` = 65k snapshots | **380 895 ms (~6.3 min)** | **92 ms (~4 100×)** |
| per-append cost, 1k → 80k records | 60 µs → ~5-10 ms (grows linearly with n) | flat **~1.5-2.3 µs** |
| bulk `appendAll` 65k | ~100 ms (already linear) | ~98 ms (unchanged) |

## Fix (algorithmic, per the card)

- **Chunked row store with copy-on-write publishing**: 512-row chunks; a snapshot publishes an immutable chunk-pointer list (O(chunks) refs); the next cycle clones a chunk before its first in-place write. Published snapshots stay byte-identical and immutable.
- **Lazy `recordLocations`**: derived on first access per snapshot (no lib/ reader touches it on the append path; identical content to the eager map).
- **Incremental requests cache**: cached sorted-fact order + built numbers + running cumulative usage; a snapshot rebuilds only the suffix at/after the first touched fact. New facts always fold in at the sorted tail (order = row count at creation, which only grows); anything the incremental path cannot prove order-stable falls back to the **exact full sort** the old code ran.
- **Streamed-row replacement** truncates a contiguous tail and drops only the cut tool-row indexes; non-tail placement keeps the legacy filter + full rebuild.

## Regression guards (bounded, not flake-prone)

- `snapshotRowCopies` counter (the `chainWalkHops` pattern, deterministic): measured **150 rows/append**, envelope 600/append — the quadratic shape copies ~n/2 rows per append and fails it by 3 orders of magnitude. No wall-clock ratio asserted: the #358 flake lesson, plus a measured 60× JIT-tier cliff on cold first runs.
- Absolute 8 s budget on a 20k live-tail run (fixed: <100 ms warm, ~2.1 s worst cold; pre-fix measured 31 s) — well under the 30 s per-test timeout cap.
- 50k `appendAll` open-budget check (issue acceptance), snapshot-immutability-under-later-appends (chunk sharing + lazy locations freeze), bulk-replay request folding (facts created + finalized between snapshots).

## Gates

- `dart analyze`: 0 issues on changed files (repo-wide 132 pre-existing infos, identical with the change stashed).
- `dart test test/trajectory/` 200 ✓ + event-handler/compaction 31 ✓ + `test/integration/trajectory/snapshot_builder_integration_test.dart` 6 ✓ (live-vs-replay requests compared field-by-field).
- `dart format` clean.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: all three card items — profile bench (1k/10k/50k/65k synthetic, growth asserted), per-append copying eliminated (structural sharing + invalidatable derived cache; `_snapshot` now O(delta)), snapshots cheap (shared refs + suffix fold; 546 ms instrumented mean → µs).
Remaining (not in scope here): the fold path itself shows a cold-run JIT-tier cliff (~100 µs/append unwarmed, ~1.7 µs warmed — same code pre/post, deterministic counters unaffected); a follow-up could warm or restructure `_appendRecord` if cold-start latency ever matters.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1504
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1504
- **Title**: perf(1497): incremental TrajectorySnapshotBuilder publishing — O(delta) per append
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1497-trajectory-append-o-n` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +595
- **Deletions**: -96
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:08:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T17:16:29Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1497

## Hot path (confirmed)

Every `append()`/`applyEvent()` materialized a snapshot by copying every ledger row (`List.of`), rebuilding the whole `recordLocations` map, and re-sorting + re-folding cumulative usage over **every** request fact — O(n) per append, O(n²) per live session. Bulk `appendAll` was already linear; the live tail was the slide-show.

**Before/after (4 records/turn synthetic, warmed VM, standalone Dart SDK 3.13.5):**

| shape | before (main @ 0c602bf47e) | after |
|---|---|---|
| live tail, 65k `append()` = 65k snapshots | **380 895 ms (~6.3 min)** | **92 ms (~4 100×)** |
| per-append cost, 1k → 80k records | 60 µs → ~5-10 ms (grows linearly with n) | flat **~1.5-2.3 µs** |
| bulk `appendAll` 65k | ~100 ms (already linear) | ~98 ms (unchanged) |

## Fix (algorithmic, per the card)

- **Chunked row store with copy-on-write publishing**: 512-row chunks; a snapshot publishes an immutable chunk-pointer list (O(chunks) refs); the next cycle clones a chunk before its first in-place write. Published snapshots stay byte-identical and immutable.
- **Lazy `recordLocations`**: derived on first access per snapshot (no lib/ reader touches it on the append path; identical content to the eager map).
- **Incremental requests cache**: cached sorted-fact order + built numbers + running cumulative usage; a snapshot rebuilds only the suffix at/after the first touched fact. New facts always fold in at the sorted tail (order = row count at creation, which only grows); anything the incremental path cannot prove order-stable falls back to the **exact full sort** the old code ran.
- **Streamed-row replacement** truncates a contiguous tail and drops only the cut tool-row indexes; non-tail placement keeps the legacy filter + full rebuild.

## Regression guards (bounded, not flake-prone)

- `snapshotRowCopies` counter (the `chainWalkHops` pattern, deterministic): measured **150 rows/append**, envelope 600/append — the quadratic shape copies ~n/2 rows per append and fails it by 3 orders of magnitude. No wall-clock ratio asserted: the #358 flake lesson, plus a measured 60× JIT-tier cliff on cold first runs.
- Absolute 8 s budget on a 20k live-tail run (fixed: <100 ms warm, ~2.1 s worst cold; pre-fix measured 31 s) — well under the 30 s per-test timeout cap.
- 50k `appendAll` open-budget check (issue acceptance), snapshot-immutability-under-later-appends (chunk sharing + lazy locations freeze), bulk-replay request folding (facts created + finalized between snapshots).

## Gates

- `dart analyze`: 0 issues on changed files (repo-wide 132 pre-existing infos, identical with the change stashed).
- `dart test test/trajectory/` 200 ✓ + event-handler/compaction 31 ✓ + `test/integration/trajectory/snapshot_builder_integration_test.dart` 6 ✓ (live-vs-replay requests compared field-by-field).
- `dart format` clean.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: all three card items — profile bench (1k/10k/50k/65k synthetic, growth asserted), per-append copying eliminated (structural sharing + invalidatable derived cache; `_snapshot` now O(delta)), snapshots cheap (shared refs + suffix fold; 546 ms instrumented mean → µs).

# pr-1504: perf(1497): incremental TrajectorySnapshotBuilder publishing — O(delta) per append

## Description

Fixes #1497

## Hot path (confirmed)

Every `append()`/`applyEvent()` materialized a snapshot by copying every ledger row (`List.of`), rebuilding the whole `recordLocations` map, and re-sorting + re-folding cumulative usage over **every** request fact — O(n) per append, O(n²) per live session. Bulk `appendAll` was already linear; the live tail was the slide-show.

**Before/after (4 records/turn synthetic, warmed VM, standalone Dart SDK 3.13.5):**

| shape | before (main @ 0c602bf47e) | after |
|---|---|---|
| live tail, 65k `append()` = 65k snapshots | **380 895 ms (~6.3 min)** | **92 ms (~4 100×)** |
| per-append cost, 1k → 80k records | 60 µs → ~5-10 ms (grows linearly with n) | flat **~1.5-2.3 µs** |
| bulk `appendAll` 65k | ~100 ms (already linear) | ~98 ms (unchanged) |

## Fix (algorithmic, per the card)

- **Chunked row store with copy-on-write publishing**: 512-row chunks; a snapshot publishes an immutable chunk-pointer list (O(chunks) refs); the next cycle clones a chunk before its first in-place write. Published snapshots stay byte-identical and immutable.
- **Lazy `recordLocations`**: derived on first access per snapshot (no lib/ reader touches it on the append path; identical content to the eager map).
- **Incremental requests cache**: cached sorted-fact order + built numbers + running cumulative usage; a snapshot rebuilds only the suffix at/after the first touched fact. New facts always fold in at the sorted tail (order = row count at creation, which only grows); anything the incremental path cannot prove order-stable falls back to the **exact full sort** the old code ran.
- **Streamed-row replacement** truncates a contiguous tail and drops only the cut tool-row indexes; non-tail placement keeps the legacy filter + full rebuild.

## Regression guards (bounded, not flake-prone)

- `snapshotRowCopies` counter (the `chainWalkHops` pattern, deterministic): measured **150 rows/append**, envelope 600/append — the quadratic shape copies ~n/2 rows per append and fails it by 3 orders of magnitude. No wall-clock ratio asserted: the #358 flake lesson, plus a measured 60× JIT-tier cliff on cold first runs.
- Absolute 8 s budget on a 20k live-tail run (fixed: <100 ms warm, ~2.1 s worst cold; pre-fix measured 31 s) — well under the 30 s per-test timeout cap.
- 50k `appendAll` open-budget check (issue acceptance), snapshot-immutability-under-later-appends (chunk sharing + lazy locations freeze), bulk-replay request folding (facts created + finalized between snapshots).

## Gates

- `dart analyze`: 0 issues on changed files (repo-wide 132 pre-existing infos, identical with the change stashed).
- `dart test test/trajectory/` 200 ✓ + event-handler/compaction 31 ✓ + `test/integration/trajectory/snapshot_builder_integration_test.dart` 6 ✓ (live-vs-replay requests compared field-by-field).
- `dart format` clean.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: all three card items — profile bench (1k/10k/50k/65k synthetic, growth asserted), per-append copying eliminated (structural sharing + invalidatable derived cache; `_snapshot` now O(delta)), snapshots cheap (shared refs + suffix fold; 546 ms instrumented mean → µs).
Remaining (not in scope here): the fold path itself shows a cold-run JIT-tier cliff (~100 µs/append unwarmed, ~1.7 µs warmed — same code pre/post, deterministic counters unaffected); a follow-up could warm or restructure `_appendRecord` if cold-start latency ever matters.

Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1504
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1504
- **Title**: perf(1497): incremental TrajectorySnapshotBuilder publishing — O(delta) per append
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1497-trajectory-append-o-n` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +595
- **Deletions**: -96
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:08:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T17:16:29Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1497

## Hot path (confirmed)

Every `append()`/`applyEvent()` materialized a snapshot by copying every ledger row (`List.of`), rebuilding the whole `recordLocations` map, and re-sorting + re-folding cumulative usage over **every** request fact — O(n) per append, O(n²) per live session. Bulk `appendAll` was already linear; the live tail was the slide-show.

**Before/after (4 records/turn synthetic, warmed VM, standalone Dart SDK 3.13.5):**

| shape | before (main @ 0c602bf47e) | after |
|---|---|---|
| live tail, 65k `append()` = 65k snapshots | **380 895 ms (~6.3 min)** | **92 ms (~4 100×)** |
| per-append cost, 1k → 80k records | 60 µs → ~5-10 ms (grows linearly with n) | flat **~1.5-2.3 µs** |
| bulk `appendAll` 65k | ~100 ms (already linear) | ~98 ms (unchanged) |

## Fix (algorithmic, per the card)

- **Chunked row store with copy-on-write publishing**: 512-row chunks; a snapshot publishes an immutable chunk-pointer list (O(chunks) refs); the next cycle clones a chunk before its first in-place write. Published snapshots stay byte-identical and immutable.
- **Lazy `recordLocations`**: derived on first access per snapshot (no lib/ reader touches it on the append path; identical content to the eager map).
- **Incremental requests cache**: cached sorted-fact order + built numbers + running cumulative usage; a snapshot rebuilds only the suffix at/after the first touched fact. New facts always fold in at the sorted tail (order = row count at creation, which only grows); anything the incremental path cannot prove order-stable falls back to the **exact full sort** the old code ran.
- **Streamed-row replacement** truncates a contiguous tail and drops only the cut tool-row indexes; non-tail placement keeps the legacy filter + full rebuild.

## Regression guards (bounded, not flake-prone)

- `snapshotRowCopies` counter (the `chainWalkHops` pattern, deterministic): measured **150 rows/append**, envelope 600/append — the quadratic shape copies ~n/2 rows per append and fails it by 3 orders of magnitude. No wall-clock ratio asserted: the #358 flake lesson, plus a measured 60× JIT-tier cliff on cold first runs.
- Absolute 8 s budget on a 20k live-tail run (fixed: <100 ms warm, ~2.1 s worst cold; pre-fix measured 31 s) — well under the 30 s per-test timeout cap.
- 50k `appendAll` open-budget check (issue acceptance), snapshot-immutability-under-later-appends (chunk sharing + lazy locations freeze), bulk-replay request folding (facts created + finalized between snapshots).

## Gates

- `dart analyze`: 0 issues on changed files (repo-wide 132 pre-existing infos, identical with the change stashed).
- `dart test test/trajectory/` 200 ✓ + event-handler/compaction 31 ✓ + `test/integration/trajectory/snapshot_builder_integration_test.dart` 6 ✓ (live-vs-replay requests compared field-by-field).
- `dart format` clean.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: all three card items — profile bench (1k/10k/50k/65k synthetic, growth asserted), per-append copying eliminated (structural sharing + invalidatable derived cache; `_snapshot` now O(delta)), snapshots cheap (shared refs + suffix fold; 546 ms instrumented mean → µs).
Remaining (not in scope here): the fold path itself shows a cold-run JIT-tier cliff (~100 µs/append unwarmed, ~1.7 µs warmed — same code pre/post, deterministic counters unaffected); a follow-up could warm or restructure `_appendRecord` if cold-start latency ever matters.

surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1504
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1504
- **Title**: perf(1497): incremental TrajectorySnapshotBuilder publishing — O(delta) per append
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1497-trajectory-append-o-n` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +595
- **Deletions**: -96
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:08:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T17:16:29Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1497

## Hot path (confirmed)

Every `append()`/`applyEvent()` materialized a snapshot by copying every ledger row (`List.of`), rebuilding the whole `recordLocations` map, and re-sorting + re-folding cumulative usage over **every** request fact — O(n) per append, O(n²) per live session. Bulk `appendAll` was already linear; the live tail was the slide-show.

**Before/after (4 records/turn synthetic, warmed VM, standalone Dart SDK 3.13.5):**

| shape | before (main @ 0c602bf47e) | after |
|---|---|---|
| live tail, 65k `append()` = 65k snapshots | **380 895 ms (~6.3 min)** | **92 ms (~4 100×)** |
| per-append cost, 1k → 80k records | 60 µs → ~5-10 ms (grows linearly with n) | flat **~1.5-2.3 µs** |
| bulk `appendAll` 65k | ~100 ms (already linear) | ~98 ms (unchanged) |

## Fix (algorithmic, per the card)

- **Chunked row store with copy-on-write publishing**: 512-row chunks; a snapshot publishes an immutable chunk-pointer list (O(chunks) refs); the next cycle clones a chunk before its first in-place write. Published snapshots stay byte-identical and immutable.
- **Lazy `recordLocations`**: derived on first access per snapshot (no lib/ reader touches it on the append path; identical content to the eager map).
- **Incremental requests cache**: cached sorted-fact order + built numbers + running cumulative usage; a snapshot rebuilds only the suffix at/after the first touched fact. New facts always fold in at the sorted tail (order = row count at creation, which only grows); anything the incremental path cannot prove order-stable falls back to the **exact full sort** the old code ran.
- **Streamed-row replacement** truncates a contiguous tail and drops only the cut tool-row indexes; non-tail placement keeps the legacy filter + full rebuild.

## Regression guards (bounded, not flake-prone)

- `snapshotRowCopies` counter (the `chainWalkHops` pattern, deterministic): measured **150 rows/append**, envelope 600/append — the quadratic shape copies ~n/2 rows per append and fails it by 3 orders of magnitude. No wall-clock ratio asserted: the #358 flake lesson, plus a measured 60× JIT-tier cliff on cold first runs.
- Absolute 8 s budget on a 20k live-tail run (fixed: <100 ms warm, ~2.1 s worst cold; pre-fix measured 31 s) — well under the 30 s per-test timeout cap.
- 50k `appendAll` open-budget check (issue acceptance), snapshot-immutability-under-later-appends (chunk sharing + lazy locations freeze), bulk-replay request folding (facts created + finalized between snapshots).

## Gates

- `dart analyze`: 0 issues on changed files (repo-wide 132 pre-existing infos, identical with the change stashed).
- `dart test test/trajectory/` 200 ✓ + event-handler/compaction 31 ✓ + `test/integration/trajectory/snapshot_builder_integration_test.dart` 6 ✓ (live-vs-replay requests compared field-by-field).
- `dart format` clean.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: all three card items — profile bench (1k/10k/50k/65k synthetic, growth asserted), per-append copying eliminated (structural sharing + invalidatable derived cache; `_snapshot` now O(delta)), snapshots cheap (shared refs + suffix fold; 546 ms instrumented mean → µs).
Remaining (not in scope here): the fold path itself shows a cold-run JIT-tier cliff (~100 µs/append unwarmed, ~1.7 µs warmed — same code pre/post, deterministic counters unaffected); a follow-up could warm or restructure `_appendRecord` if cold-start latency ever matters.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1504
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1504
- **Title**: perf(1497): incremental TrajectorySnapshotBuilder publishing — O(delta) per append
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1497-trajectory-append-o-n` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +595
- **Deletions**: -96
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:08:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T17:16:29Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1497

## Hot path (confirmed)

Every `append()`/`applyEvent()` materialized a snapshot by copying every ledger row (`List.of`), rebuilding the whole `recordLocations` map, and re-sorting + re-folding cumulative usage over **every** request fact — O(n) per append, O(n²) per live session. Bulk `appendAll` was already linear; the live tail was the slide-show.

**Before/after (4 records/turn synthetic, warmed VM, standalone Dart SDK 3.13.5):**

| shape | before (main @ 0c602bf47e) | after |
|---|---|---|
| live tail, 65k `append()` = 65k snapshots | **380 895 ms (~6.3 min)** | **92 ms (~4 100×)** |
| per-append cost, 1k → 80k records | 60 µs → ~5-10 ms (grows linearly with n) | flat **~1.5-2.3 µs** |
| bulk `appendAll` 65k | ~100 ms (already linear) | ~98 ms (unchanged) |

## Fix (algorithmic, per the card)

- **Chunked row store with copy-on-write publishing**: 512-row chunks; a snapshot publishes an immutable chunk-pointer list (O(chunks) refs); the next cycle clones a chunk before its first in-place write. Published snapshots stay byte-identical and immutable.
- **Lazy `recordLocations`**: derived on first access per snapshot (no lib/ reader touches it on the append path; identical content to the eager map).
- **Incremental requests cache**: cached sorted-fact order + built numbers + running cumulative usage; a snapshot rebuilds only the suffix at/after the first touched fact. New facts always fold in at the sorted tail (order = row count at creation, which only grows); anything the incremental path cannot prove order-stable falls back to the **exact full sort** the old code ran.
- **Streamed-row replacement** truncates a contiguous tail and drops only the cut tool-row indexes; non-tail placement keeps the legacy filter + full rebuild.

## Regression guards (bounded, not flake-prone)

- `snapshotRowCopies` counter (the `chainWalkHops` pattern, deterministic): measured **150 rows/append**, envelope 600/append — the quadratic shape copies ~n/2 rows per append and fails it by 3 orders of magnitude. # pr-1504: perf(1497): incremental TrajectorySnapshotBuilder publishing — O(delta) per append

## Description

Fixes #1497

## Hot path (confirmed)

Every `append()`/`applyEvent()` materialized a snapshot by copying every ledger row (`List.of`), rebuilding the whole `recordLocations` map, and re-sorting + re-folding cumulative usage over **every** request fact — O(n) per append, O(n²) per live session. Bulk `appendAll` was already linear; the live tail was the slide-show.

**Before/after (4 records/turn synthetic, warmed VM, standalone Dart SDK 3.13.5):**

| shape | before (main @ 0c602bf47e) | after |
|---|---|---|
| live tail, 65k `append()` = 65k snapshots | **380 895 ms (~6.3 min)** | **92 ms (~4 100×)** |
| per-append cost, 1k → 80k records | 60 µs → ~5-10 ms (grows linearly with n) | flat **~1.5-2.3 µs** |
| bulk `appendAll` 65k | ~100 ms (already linear) | ~98 ms (unchanged) |

## Fix (algorithmic, per the card)

- **Chunked row store with copy-on-write publishing**: 512-row chunks; a snapshot publishes an immutable chunk-pointer list (O(chunks) refs); the next cycle clones a chunk before its first in-place write. Published snapshots stay byte-identical and immutable.
- **Lazy `recordLocations`**: derived on first access per snapshot (no lib/ reader touches it on the append path; identical content to the eager map).
- **Incremental requests cache**: cached sorted-fact order + built numbers + running cumulative usage; a snapshot rebuilds only the suffix at/after the first touched fact. New facts always fold in at the sorted tail (order = row count at creation, which only grows); anything the incremental path cannot prove order-stable falls back to the **exact full sort** the old code ran.
- **Streamed-row replacement** truncates a contiguous tail and drops only the cut tool-row indexes; non-tail placement keeps the legacy filter + full rebuild.

## Regression guards (bounded, not flake-prone)

- `snapshotRowCopies` counter (the `chainWalkHops` pattern, deterministic): measured **150 rows/append**, envelope 600/append — the quadratic shape copies ~n/2 rows per append and fails it by 3 orders of magnitude. No wall-clock ratio asserted: the #358 flake lesson, plus a measured 60× JIT-tier cliff on cold first runs.
- Absolute 8 s budget on a 20k live-tail run (fixed: <100 ms warm, ~2.1 s worst cold; pre-fix measured 31 s) — well under the 30 s per-test timeout cap.
- 50k `appendAll` open-budget check (issue acceptance), snapshot-immutability-under-later-appends (chunk sharing + lazy locations freeze), bulk-replay request folding (facts created + finalized between snapshots).

## Gates

- `dart analyze`: 0 issues on changed files (repo-wide 132 pre-existing infos, identical with the change stashed).
- `dart test test/trajectory/` 200 ✓ + event-handler/compaction 31 ✓ + `test/integration/trajectory/snapshot_builder_integration_test.dart` 6 ✓ (live-vs-replay requests compared field-by-field).
- `dart format` clean.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: all three card items — profile bench (1k/10k/50k/65k synthetic, growth asserted), per-append copying eliminated (structural sharing + invalidatable derived cache; `_snapshot` now O(delta)), snapshots cheap (shared refs + suffix fold; 546 ms instrumented mean → µs).
Remaining (not in scope here): the fold path itself shows a cold-run JIT-tier cliff (~100 µs/append unwarmed, ~1.7 µs warmed — same code pre/post, deterministic counters unaffected); a follow-up could warm or restructure `_appendRecord` if cold-start latency ever matters.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1504
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1504
- **Title**: perf(1497): incremental TrajectorySnapshotBuilder publishing — O(delta) per append
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1497-trajectory-append-o-n` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +595
- **Deletions**: -96
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:08:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T17:16:29Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1497

## Hot path (confirmed)

Every `append()`/`applyEvent()` materialized a snapshot by copying every ledger row (`List.of`), rebuilding the whole `recordLocations` map, and re-sorting + re-folding cumulative usage over **every** request fact — O(n) per append, O(n²) per live session. Bulk `appendAll` was already linear; the live tail was the slide-show.

**Before/after (4 records/turn synthetic, warmed VM, standalone Dart SDK 3.13.5):**

| shape | before (main @ 0c602bf47e) | after |
|---|---|---|
| live tail, 65k `append()` = 65k snapshots | **380 895 ms (~6.3 min)** | **92 ms (~4 100×)** |
| per-append cost, 1k → 80k records | 60 µs → ~5-10 ms (grows linearly with n) | flat **~1.5-2.3 µs** |
| bulk `appendAll` 65k | ~100 ms (already linear) | ~98 ms (unchanged) |

## Fix (algorithmic, per the card)

- **Chunked row store with copy-on-write publishing**: 512-row chunks; a snapshot publishes an immutable chunk-pointer list (O(chunks) refs); the next cycle clones a chunk before its first in-place write. Published snapshots stay byte-identical and immutable.
- **Lazy `recordLocations`**: derived on first access per snapshot (no lib/ reader touches it on the append path; identical content to the eager map).
- **Incremental requests cache**: cached sorted-fact order + built numbers + running cumulative usage; a snapshot rebuilds only the suffix at/after the first touched fact. New facts always fold in at the sorted tail (order = row count at creation, which only grows); anything the incremental path cannot prove order-stable falls back to the **exact full sort** the old code ran.
- **Streamed-row replacement** truncates a contiguous tail and drops only the cut tool-row indexes; non-tail placement keeps the legacy filter + full rebuild.

## Regression guards (bounded, not flake-prone)

- `snapshotRowCopies` counter (the `chainWalkHops` pattern, deterministic): measured **150 rows/append**, envelope 600/append — the quadratic shape copies ~n/2 rows per append and fails it by 3 orders of magnitude. No wall-clock ratio asserted: the #358 flake lesson, plus a measured 60× JIT-tier cliff on cold first runs.
- Absolute 8 s budget on a 20k live-tail run (fixed: <100 ms warm, ~2.1 s worst cold; pre-fix measured 31 s) — well under the 30 s per-test timeout cap.
- 50k `appendAll` open-budget check (issue acceptance), snapshot-immutability-under-later-appends (chunk sharing + lazy locations freeze), bulk-replay request folding (facts created + finalized between snapshots).

## Gates

- `dart analyze`: 0 issues on changed files (repo-wide 132 pre-existing infos, identical with the change stashed).
- `dart test test/trajectory/` 200 ✓ + event-handler/compaction 31 ✓ + `test/integration/trajectory/snapshot_builder_integration_test.dart` 6 ✓ (live-vs-replay requests compared field-by-field).
- `dart format` clean.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: all three card items — profile bench (1k/10k/50k/65k synthetic, growth asserted), per-append copying eliminated (structural sharing + invalidatable derived cache; `_snapshot` now O(delta)), snapshots cheap (shared refs + suffix fold; 546 ms instrumented mean → µs).
Remaining (not in scope here): the fold path itself shows a cold-run JIT-tier cliff (~100 µs/append unwarmed, ~1.7 µs warmed — same code pre/post, deterministic counters unaffected); a follow-up could warm or restructure `_appendRecord` if cold-start latency ever matters.

Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1504
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1504
- **Title**: perf(1497): incremental TrajectorySnapshotBuilder publishing — O(delta) per append
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1497-trajectory-append-o-n` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +595
- **Deletions**: -96
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:08:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T17:16:29Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1497

## Hot path (confirmed)

Every `append()`/`applyEvent()` materialized a snapshot by copying every ledger row (`List.of`), rebuilding the whole `recordLocations` map, and re-sorting + re-folding cumulative usage over **every** request fact — O(n) per append, O(n²) per live session. Bulk `appendAll` was already linear; the live tail was the slide-show.

**Before/after (4 records/turn synthetic, warmed VM, standalone Dart SDK 3.13.5):**

| shape | before (main @ 0c602bf47e) | after |
|---|---|---|
| live tail, 65k `append()` = 65k snapshots | **380 895 ms (~6.3 min)** | **92 ms (~4 100×)** |
| per-append cost, 1k → 80k records | 60 µs → ~5-10 ms (grows linearly with n) | flat **~1.5-2.3 µs** |
| bulk `appendAll` 65k | ~100 ms (already linear) | ~98 ms (unchanged) |

## Fix (algorithmic, per the card)

- **Chunked row store with copy-on-write publishing**: 512-row chunks; a snapshot publishes an immutable chunk-pointer list (O(chunks) refs); the next cycle clones a chunk before its first in-place write. Published snapshots stay byte-identical and immutable.
- **Lazy `recordLocations`**: derived on first access per snapshot (no lib/ reader touches it on the append path; identical content to the eager map).
- **Incremental requests cache**: cached sorted-fact order + built numbers + running cumulative usage; a snapshot rebuilds only the suffix at/after the first touched fact. New facts always fold in at the sorted tail (order = row count at creation, which only grows); anything the incremental path cannot prove order-stable falls back to the **exact full sort** the old code ran.
- **Streamed-row replacement** truncates a contiguous tail and drops only the cut tool-row indexes; non-tail placement keeps the legacy filter + full rebuild.

## Regression guards (bounded, not flake-prone)

- `snapshotRowCopies` counter (the `chainWalkHops` pattern, deterministic): measured **150 rows/append**, envelope 600/append — the quadratic shape copies ~n/2 rows per append and fails it by 3 orders of magnitude. No wall-clock ratio asserted: the #358 flake lesson, plus a measured 60× JIT-tier cliff on cold first runs.
- Absolute 8 s budget on a 20k live-tail run (fixed: <100 ms warm, ~2.1 s worst cold; pre-fix measured 31 s) — well under the 30 s per-test timeout cap.
- 50k `appendAll` open-budget check (issue acceptance), snapshot-immutability-under-later-appends (chunk sharing + lazy locations freeze), bulk-replay request folding (facts created + finalized between snapshots).

## Gates

- `dart analyze`: 0 issues on changed files (repo-wide 132 pre-existing infos, identical with the change stashed).
- `dart test test/trajectory/` 200 ✓ + event-handler/compaction 31 ✓ + `test/integration/trajectory/snapshot_builder_integration_test.dart` 6 ✓ (live-vs-replay requests compared field-by-field).
- `dart format` clean.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: all three card items — profile bench (1k/10k/50k/65k synthetic, growth asserted), per-append copying eliminated (structural sharing + invalidatable derived cache; `_snapshot` now O(delta)), snapshots cheap (shared refs + suffix fold; 546 ms instrumented mean → µs).
Remaining (not in scope here): the fold path itself shows a cold-run JIT-tier cliff (~100 µs/append unwarmed, ~1.7 µs warmed — same code pre/post, deterministic counters unaffected); a follow-up could warm or restructure `_appendRecord` if cold-start latency ever matters.

DMTools CLI Wrapper

Usage:
  dmtools list                           # List available MCP tools
  dmtools doctor                         # Check current directory configuration
  dmtools run <json-file>                # Execute job with JSON config file
  dmtools run <job-name> [--key value]   # Execute a registered job without a config file
  dmtools run <json-file> <encoded>      # Execute job with file + encoded overrides
  dmtools <tool> [args...]              # Execute MCP tool with args
  dmtools <tool> --data '{"json"}'      # Execute with inline JSON
  dmtools <tool> --file params.json     # Execute with JSON file
  dmtools <tool> --verbose              # Execute with verbose output
  dmtools <tool> --debug                # Execute with debug output and error messages
  dmtools <tool> <<EOF                  # Execute with heredoc
  {"json": "data"}
  EOF

Examples:
  dmtools list
  dmtools doctor
  dmtools run job-config.json
  dmtools run codegenerator --param1 test
  dmtools jira_get_ticket DMC-479 summary,description
  dmtools jira_get_ticket --data '{"key": "DMC-479", "fields": ["summary"]}'

Environment Variables:
  DMTOOLS_INTEGRATIONS    Comma-separated list of integrations (jira,confluence,figma)

Environment Files:
  The tool automatically loads environment variables from dmtools.env

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1504
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1504
- **Title**: perf(1497): incremental TrajectorySnapshotBuilder publishing — O(delta) per append
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1497-trajectory-append-o-n` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +595
- **Deletions**: -96
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:08:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T17:16:29Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1497

## Hot path (confirmed)

Every `append()`/`applyEvent()` materialized a snapshot by copying every ledger row (`List.of`), rebuilding the whole `recordLocations` map, and re-sorting + re-folding cumulative usage over **every** request fact — O(n) per append, O(n²) per live session. Bulk `appendAll` was already linear; the live tail was the slide-show.

**Before/after (4 records/turn synthetic, warmed VM, standalone Dart SDK 3.13.5):**

| shape | before (main @ 0c602bf47e) | after |
|---|---|---|
| live tail, 65k `append()` = 65k snapshots | **380 895 ms (~6.3 min)** | **92 ms (~4 100×)** |
| per-append cost, 1k → 80k records | 60 µs → ~5-10 ms (grows linearly with n) | flat **~1.5-2.3 µs** |
| bulk `appendAll` 65k | ~100 ms (already linear) | ~98 ms (unchanged) |

## Fix (algorithmic, per the card)

- **Chunked row store with copy-on-write publishing**: 512-row chunks; a snapshot publishes an immutable chunk-pointer list (O(chunks) refs); the next cycle clones a chunk before its first in-place write. Published snapshots stay byte-identical and immutable.
- **Lazy `recordLocations`**: derived on first access per snapshot (no lib/ reader touches it on the append path; identical content to the eager map).
- **Incremental requests cache**: cached sorted-fact order + built numbers + running cumulative usage; a snapshot rebuilds only the suffix at/after the first touched fact. New facts always fold in at the sorted tail (order = row count at creation, which only grows); anything the incremental path cannot prove order-stable falls back to the **exact full sort** the old code ran.
- **Streamed-row replacement** truncates a contiguous tail and drops only the cut tool-row indexes; non-tail placement keeps the legacy filter + full rebuild.

## Regression guards (bounded, not flake-prone)

- `snapshotRowCopies` counter (the `chainWalkHops` pattern, deterministic): measured **150 rows/append**, envelope 600/append — the quadratic shape copies ~n/2 rows per append and fails it by 3 orders of magnitude. No wall-clock ratio asserted: the #358 flake lesson, plus a measured 60× JIT-tier cliff on cold first runs.
- Absolute 8 s budget on a 20k live-tail run (fixed: <100 ms warm, ~2.1 s worst cold; pre-fix measured 31 s) — well under the 30 s per-test timeout cap.
- 50k `appendAll` open-budget check (issue acceptance), snapshot-immutability-under-later-appends (chunk sharing + lazy locations freeze), bulk-replay request folding (facts created + finalized between snapshots).

## Gates

- `dart analyze`: 0 issues on changed files (repo-wide 132 pre-existing infos, identical with the change stashed).
- `dart test test/trajectory/` 200 ✓ + event-handler/compaction 31 ✓ + `test/integration/trajectory/snapshot_builder_integration_test.dart` 6 ✓ (live-vs-replay requests compared field-by-field).
- `dart format` clean.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: all three card items — profile bench (1k/10k/50k/65k synthetic, growth asserted), per-append copying eliminated (structural sharing + invalidatable derived cache; `_snapshot` now O(delta)), snapshots cheap (shared refs + suffix fold; 546 ms instrumented mean → µs).
Remaining (not in scope here): the fold path itself shows a cold-run JIT-tier cliff (~100 µs/append unwarmed, ~1.7 µs warmed — same code pre/post, deterministic counters unaffected); a follow-up could warm or restructure `_appendRecord` if cold-start latency ever matters.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1504
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1504
- **Title**: perf(1497): incremental TrajectorySnapshotBuilder publishing — O(delta) per append
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1497-trajectory-append-o-n` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +595
- **Deletions**: -96
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:08:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T17:16:29Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1497

## Hot path (confirmed)

Every `append()`/`applyEvent()` materialized a snapshot by copying every ledger row (`List.of`), rebuilding the whole `recordLocations` map, and re-sorting + re-folding cumulative usage over **every** request fact — O(n) per append, O(n²) per live session. Bulk `appendAll` was already linear; the live tail was the slide-show.

**Before/after (4 records/turn synthetic, warmed VM, standalone Dart SDK 3.13.5):**

| shape | before (main @ 0c602bf47e) | after |
|---|---|---|
| live tail, 65k `append()` = 65k snapshots | **380 895 ms (~6.3 min)** | **92 ms (~4 100×)** |
| per-append cost, 1k → 80k records | 60 µs → ~5-10 ms (grows linearly with n) | flat **~1.5-2.3 µs** |
| bulk `appendAll` 65k | ~100 ms (already linear) | ~98 ms (unchanged) |

## Fix (algorithmic, per the card)

- **Chunked row store with copy-on-write publishing**: 512-row chunks; a snapshot publishes an immutable chunk-pointer list (O(chunks) refs); the next cycle clones a chunk before its first in-place write. Published snapshots stay byte-identical and immutable.
- **Lazy `recordLocations`**: derived on first access per snapshot (no lib/ reader touches it on the append path; identical content to the eager map).
- **Incremental requests cache**: cached sorted-fact order + built numbers + running cumulative usage; a snapshot rebuilds only the suffix at/after the first touched fact. New facts always fold in at the sorted tail (order = row count at creation, which only grows); anything the incremental path cannot prove order-stable falls back to the **exact full sort** the old code ran.
- **Streamed-row replacement** truncates a contiguous tail and drops only the cut tool-row indexes; non-tail placement keeps the legacy filter + full rebuild.

## Regression guards (bounded, not flake-prone)

- `snapshotRowCopies` counter (the `chainWalkHops` pattern, deterministic): measured **150 rows/append**, envelope 600/append — the quadratic shape copies ~n/2 rows per append and fails it by 3 orders of magnitude. No wall-clock ratio asserted: the #358 flake lesson, plus a measured 60× JIT-tier cliff on cold first runs.
- Absolute 8 s budget on a 20k live-tail run (fixed: <100 ms warm, ~2.1 s worst cold; pre-fix measured 31 s) — well under the 30 s per-test timeout cap.
- 50k `appendAll` open-budget check (issue acceptance), snapshot-immutability-under-later-appends (chunk sharing + lazy locations freeze), bulk-replay request folding (facts created + finalized between snapshots).

## Gates

- `dart analyze`: 0 issues on changed files (repo-wide 132 pre-existing infos, identical with the change stashed).
- `dart test test/trajectory/` 200 ✓ + event-handler/compaction 31 ✓ + `test/integration/trajectory/snapshot_builder_integration_test.dart` 6 ✓ (live-vs-replay requests compared field-by-field).
- `dart format` clean.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: all three card items — profile bench (1k/10k/50k/65k synthetic, growth asserted), per-append copying eliminated (structural sharing + invalidatable derived cache; `_snapshot` now O(delta)), snapshots cheap (shared refs + suffix fold; 546 ms instrumented mean → µs).
Remaining (not in scope here): the fold path itself shows a cold-run JIT-tier cliff (~100 µs/append unwarmed, ~1.7 µs warmed — same code pre/post, deterministic counters unaffected); a follow-up could warm or restructure `_appendRecord` if cold-start latency ever matters.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1504
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1504
- **Title**: perf(1497): incremental TrajectorySnapshotBuilder publishing — O(delta) per append
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1497-trajectory-append-o-n` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +595
- **Deletions**: -96
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:08:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T17:16:29Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1497

## Hot path (confirmed)

Every `append()`/`applyEvent()` materialized a snapshot by copying every ledger row (`List.of`), rebuilding the whole `recordLocations` map, and re-sorting + re-folding cumulative usage over **every** request fact — O(n) per append, O(n²) per live session. Bulk `appendAll` was already linear; the live tail was the slide-show.

**Before/after (4 records/turn synthetic, warmed VM, standalone Dart SDK 3.13.5):**

| shape | before (main @ 0c602bf47e) | after |
|---|---|---|
| live tail, 65k `append()` = 65k snapshots | **380 895 ms (~6.3 min)** | **92 ms (~4 100×)** |
| per-append cost, 1k → 80k records | 60 µs → ~5-10 ms (grows linearly with n) | flat **~1.5-2.3 µs** |
| bulk `appendAll` 65k | ~100 ms (already linear) | ~98 ms (unchanged) |

## Fix (algorithmic, per the card)

- **Chunked row store with copy-on-write publishing**: 512-row chunks; a snapshot publishes an immutable chunk-pointer list (O(chunks) refs); the next cycle clones a chunk before its first in-place write. Published snapshots stay byte-identical and immutable.

New facts always fold in at the sorted tail (order = row count at creation, which only grows); anything the incremental path cannot prove order-stable falls back to the **exact full sort** the old code ran.

## Regression guards (bounded, not flake-prone)

- `snapshotRowCopies` counter (the `chainWalkHops` pattern, deterministic): measured **150 rows/append**, envelope 600/append — the quadratic shape copies ~n/2 rows per append and fails it by 3 orders of magnitude. - 50k `appendAll` open-budget check (issue acceptance), snapshot-immutability-under-later-appends (chunk sharing + lazy locations freeze), bulk-replay request folding (facts created + finalized between snapshots).

- `dart analyze`: 0 issues on changed files (repo-wide 132 pre-existing infos, identical with the change stashed).

- `dart format` clean.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: all three card items — profile bench (1k/10k/50k/65k synthetic, growth asserted), per-append copying eliminated (structural sharing + invalidatable derived cache; `_snapshot` now O(delta)), snapshots cheap (shared refs + suffix fold; 546 ms instrumented mean → µs).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1504
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1504
- **Title**: perf(1497): incremental TrajectorySnapshotBuilder publishing — O(delta) per append
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1497-trajectory-append-o-n` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +595
- **Deletions**: -96
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:08:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T17:16:29Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1497

## Hot path (confirmed)

Every `append()`/`applyEvent()` materialized a snapshot by copying every ledger row (`List.of`), rebuilding the whole `recordLocations` map, and re-sorting + re-folding cumulative usage over **every** request fact — O(n) per append, O(n²) per live session. Bulk `appendAll` was already linear; the live tail was the slide-show.

**Before/after (4 records/turn synthetic, warmed VM, standalone Dart SDK 3.13.5):**

| shape | before (main @ 0c602bf47e) | after |
|---|---|---|
| live tail, 65k `append()` = 65k snapshots | **380 895 ms (~6.3 min)** | **92 ms (~4 100×)** |
| per-append cost, 1k → 80k records | 60 µs → ~5-10 ms (grows linearly with n) | flat **~1.5-2.3 µs** |
| bulk `appendAll` 65k | ~100 ms (already linear) | ~98 ms (unchanged) |

## Fix (algorithmic, per the card)

- **Chunked row store with copy-on-write publishing**: 512-row chunks; a snapshot publishes an immutable chunk-pointer list (O(chunks) refs); the next cycle clones a chunk before its first in-place write. Published snapshots stay byte-identical and immutable.
- **Lazy `recordLocations`**: derived on first access per snapshot (no lib/ reader touches it on the append path; identical content to the eager map).
- **Incremental requests cache**: cached sorted-fact order + built numbers + running cumulative usage; a snapshot rebuilds only the suffix at/after the first touched fact. New facts always fold in at the sorted tail (order = row count at creation, which only grows); anything the incremental path cannot prove order-stable falls back to the **exact full sort** the old code ran.
- **Streamed-row replacement** truncates a contiguous tail and drops only the cut tool-row indexes; non-tail placement keeps the legacy filter + full rebuild.

## Regression guards (bounded, not flake-prone)

- `snapshotRowCopies` counter (the `chainWalkHops` pattern, deterministic): measured **150 rows/append**, envelope 600/append — the quadratic shape copies ~n/2 rows per append and fails it by 3 orders of magnitude. No wall-clock ratio asserted: the #358 flake lesson, plus a measured 60× JIT-tier cliff on cold first runs.
- Absolute 8 s budget on a 20k live-tail run (fixed: <100 ms warm, ~2.1 s worst cold; pre-fix measured 31 s) — well under the 30 s per-test timeout cap.
- 50k `appendAll` open-budget check (issue acceptance), snapshot-immutability-under-later-appends (chunk sharing + lazy locations freeze), bulk-replay request folding (facts created + finalized between snapshots).

## Gates

- `dart analyze`: 0 issues on changed files (repo-wide 132 pre-existing infos, identical with the change stashed).
- `dart test test/trajectory/` 200 ✓ + event-handler/compaction 31 ✓ + `test/integration/trajectory/snapshot_builder_integration_test.dart` 6 ✓ (live-vs-replay requests compared field-by-field).
- `dart format` clean.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: all three card items — profile bench (1k/10k/50k/65k synthetic, growth asserted), per-append copying eliminated (structural sharing + invalidatable derived cache; `_snapshot` now O(delta)), snapshots cheap (shared refs + suffix fold; 546 ms instrumented mean → µs).
Remaining (not in scope here): the fold path itself shows a cold-run JIT-tier cliff (~100 µs/append unwarmed, ~1.7 µs warmed — same code pre/post, deterministic counters unaffected); a follow-up could warm or restructure `_appendRecord` if cold-start latency ever matters.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1504
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1504
- **Title**: perf(1497): incremental TrajectorySnapshotBuilder publishing — O(delta) per append
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1497-trajectory-append-o-n` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +595
- **Deletions**: -96
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:08:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T17:16:29Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1497

## Hot path (confirmed)

Every `append()`/`applyEvent()` materialized a snapshot by copying every ledger row (`List.of`), rebuilding the whole `recordLocations` map, and re-sorting + re-folding cumulative usage over **every** request fact — O(n) per append, O(n²) per live session. Bulk `appendAll` was already linear; the live tail was the slide-show.

**Before/after (4 records/turn synthetic, warmed VM, standalone Dart SDK 3.13.5):**

| shape | before (main @ 0c602bf47e) | after |
|---|---|---|
| live tail, 65k `append()` = 65k snapshots | **380 895 ms (~6.3 min)** | **92 ms (~4 100×)** |
| per-append cost, 1k → 80k records | 60 µs → ~5-10 ms (grows linearly with n) | flat **~1.5-2.3 µs** |
| bulk `appendAll` 65k | ~100 ms (already linear) | ~98 ms (unchanged) |

## Fix (algorithmic, per the card)

- **Chunked row store with copy-on-write publishing**: 512-row chunks; a snapshot publishes an immutable chunk-pointer list (O(chunks) refs); the next cycle clones a chunk before its first in-place write. Published snapshots stay byte-identical and immutable.
- **Lazy `recordLocations`**: derived on first access per snapshot (no lib/ reader touches it on the append path; identical content to the eager map).
- **Incremental requests cache**: cached sorted-fact order + built numbers + running cumulative usage; a snapshot rebuilds only the suffix at/after the first touched fact. New facts always fold in at the sorted tail (order = row count at creation, which only grows); anything the incremental path cannot prove order-stable falls back to the **exact full sort** the old code ran.
- **Streamed-row replacement** truncates a contiguous tail and drops only the cut tool-row indexes; non-tail placement keeps the legacy filter + full rebuild.

## Regression guards (bounded, not flake-prone)

- `snapshotRowCopies` counter (the `chainWalkHops` pattern, deterministic): measured **150 rows/append**, envelope 600/append — the quadratic shape copies ~n/2 rows per append and fails it by 3 orders of magnitude. No wall-clock ratio asserted: the #358 flake lesson, plus a measured 60× JIT-tier cliff on cold first runs.
- Absolute 8 s budget on a 20k live-tail run (fixed: <100 ms warm, ~2.1 s worst cold; pre-fix measured 31 s) — well under the 30 s per-test timeout cap.
- 50k `appendAll` open-budget check (issue acceptance), snapshot-immutability-under-later-appends (chunk sharing + lazy locations freeze), bulk-replay request folding (facts created + finalized between snapshots).

## Gates

blocks.text:
# pr-1504: perf(1497): incremental TrajectorySnapshotBuilder publishing — O(delta) per append

## Description

Fixes #1497

## Hot path (confirmed)

Every `append()`/`applyEvent()` materialized a snapshot by copying every ledger row (`List.of`), rebuilding the whole `recordLocations` map, and re-sorting + re-folding cumulative usage over **every** request fact — O(n) per append, O(n²) per live session. Bulk `appendAll` was already linear; the live tail was the slide-show.

**Before/after (4 records/turn synthetic, warmed VM, standalone Dart SDK 3.13.5):**

| shape | before (main @ 0c602bf47e) | after |
|---|---|---|
| live tail, 65k `append()` = 65k snapshots | **380 895 ms (~6.3 min)** | **92 ms (~4 100×)** |
| per-append cost, 1k → 80k records | 60 µs → ~5-10 ms (grows linearly with n) | flat **~1.5-2.3 µs** |
| bulk `appendAll` 65k | ~100 ms (already linear) | ~98 ms (unchanged) |

## Fix (algorithmic, per the card)

- **Chunked row store with copy-on-write publishing**: 512-row chunks; a snapshot publishes an immutable chunk-pointer list (O(chunks) refs); the next cycle clones a chunk before its first in-place write. Published snapshots stay byte-identical and immutable.
- **Lazy `recordLocations`**: derived on first access per snapshot (no lib/ reader touches it on the append path; identical content to the eager map).
- **Incremental requests cache**: cached sorted-fact order + built numbers + running cumulative usage; a snapshot rebuilds only the suffix at/after the first touched fact. New facts always fold in at the sorted tail (order = row count at creation, which only grows); anything the incremental path cannot prove order-stable falls back to the **exact full sort** the old code ran.
- **Streamed-row replacement** truncates a contiguous tail and drops only the cut tool-row indexes; non-tail placement keeps the legacy filter + full rebuild.

## Regression guards (bounded, not flake-prone)

- `snapshotRowCopies` counter (the `chainWalkHops` pattern, deterministic): measured **150 rows/append**, envelope 600/append — the quadratic shape copies ~n/2 rows per append and fails it by 3 orders of magnitude. No wall-clock ratio asserted: the #358 flake lesson, plus a measured 60× JIT-tier cliff on cold first runs.
- Absolute 8 s budget on a 20k live-tail run (fixed: <100 ms warm, ~2.1 s worst cold; pre-fix measured 31 s) — well under the 30 s per-test timeout cap.
- 50k `appendAll` open-budget check (issue acceptance), snapshot-immutability-under-later-appends (chunk sharing + lazy locations freeze), bulk-replay request folding (facts created + finalized between snapshots).

## Gates

- `dart analyze`: 0 issues on changed files (repo-wide 132 pre-existing infos, identical with the change stashed).
- `dart test test/trajectory/` 200 ✓ + event-handler/compaction 31 ✓ + `test/integration/trajectory/snapshot_builder_integration_test.dart` 6 ✓ (live-vs-replay requests compared field-by-field).
- `dart format` clean.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: all three card items — profile bench (1k/10k/50k/65k synthetic, growth asserted), per-append copying eliminated (structural sharing + invalidatable derived cache; `_snapshot` now O(delta)), snapshots cheap (shared refs + suffix fold; 546 ms instrumented mean → µs).
Remaining (not in scope here): the fold path itself shows a cold-run JIT-tier cliff (~100 µs/append unwarmed, ~1.7 µs warmed — same code pre/post, deterministic counters unaffected); a follow-up could warm or restructure `_appendRecord` if cold-start latency ever matters.

blocks.text:
Found the real CI failure. It's a REAL regression caused by this PR:

Test: `test/integration/trajectory/cli_integration_test.dart` — "cost prints the usage table with the cumulative line".

Expected: `session cumulative: in 400` (i.e., cumulative across all requests = 100+100+200 = 400 input tokens).

Actual: `session cumulative: in 200, out 40, tokens 240, cost $0.0300` — the last request's usage only, not the cumulative over all requests.

Wait, look at the table:
```
#  turn/step  model        in  out  total     cost
1  1/1        mock-model  100   20    120  $0.0100
2  1/2        mock-model  100   20    120  $0.0100
3  1/0        —             —    —      —        —
4  2/1        mock-model  200   40    240  $0.0300
session cumulative: in 200, out 40, tokens 240, cost $0.0300
```

Interesting — row 4's cost shows $0.0300, and per-request costs... cumulative line shows in 200 = only the last row. Expected in 400 (100+100+200). So the cumulative usage is being recomputed incorrectly — the suffix fold lost the earlier facts' contributions.

Why? Look at the flow: the builder gets per-append snapshots (live tail). Facts get created/touched. Let's think about the scenario:

- Turn 1/1 assistant completes with usage (100/20): facts created with order=_rows.length at completion → `_requestFactAdded`.
- Turn 1/2: another.
- A summary/system record (1/0 shows '—', purpose maybe system? No — purpose empty/turn 1 step 0, that looks like an assistant fact that never completed? Actually row 3 shows no model and '—' values: a running fact or a request without usage).
- Turn 2/1 with usage 200/40.

The cumulative: expected sums all usages = 400. Got 200 → only the last fact folded.

What could go wrong in the incremental path? Consider fact creation via `_requestFactAdded`, then `_requestFactTouched` later... The touched path: `_reqPositions[fact]` position found, sets `_reqDirtyFrom = position`. Then `_rebuildRequestsSuffix(from)` starts cumulative from `_reqCumulative[from-1]`. Looks right.

But here's a bug: in `_requestFactTouched`, when the touched fact is NOT yet in positions (created after last publish), position == null → return; only dirty set. Fine.

Real bug candidate: **facts that get REUSED via the "existing" path in `_noteAssistantMessage`**:

```dart
final existing = _assistantRequests[key];
if (existing != null) {
  existing
    ..provider = message.provider
    ..model = message.model
    ..startedAt ??= message.timestamp;
  _requestFactTouched(existing);
  return;
}
```

Hmm.

Another candidate: `_assistantRequests[key]` facts are also mutated by `_stampSystemHashes`? No.

Let me think about the actual scenario in the integration test. Better: let me look at the test to understand the record flow, and reproduce locally. Actually, better to just run the failing test locally on the PR branch.

Actually let me think about the deeper bug. The cumulative "in 200" = only the last request. Rows 1,2 have usage 100/20 each; row 3 none; row 4 200/40. Expected cumulative = 400/60/460? Expected 'in 400'. Got 'in 200'. So `_reqCumulative` at the end only included fact 4's usage.

Hypothesis: `_reqSorted` got replaced/resorted such that earlier facts dropped? No — rows 1,2,3 appear in the table, so all facts present with correct per-request usage. Only cumulative is wrong. The cumulative of the last row = 200 means `_foldRequestNumber` seeded cumulative from zero at row 4's position, i.e., `_rebuildRequestsSuffix(3)` seeded `cumulative = _reqCumulative[2]` — and `_reqCumulative[2]` was null (or stale) instead of 120.

When could `_reqCumulative` be out of sync? `_rebuildAllRequests` resets it. `_foldRequestNumber` writes index i. `_rebuildRequestsSuffix(from)` seeds from `from == 0 ? null : _reqCumulative[from - 1]`.

Bug scenario: `_reqDirtyFrom` = position of touched fact, but `_reqCumulative` could have been built at a time when fewer facts existed. Suppose at publish N, sorted had 3 facts, `_reqCumulative` has length 3. Then a 4th fact added → `_requestFactAdded`. Then publish N+1: `_insertAddedRequests` appends fact 4 to sorted (len 4), `_reqDirtyFrom` is _reqUntouched → from = min(_reqUntouched, _reqNumberRows.length=3) = 3 → `_rebuildRequestsSuffix(3)` seeds from `_reqCumulative[2]` = 120, folds fact 4 → 320. That's correct.

But what if between publish N and N+1, an EARLIER fact was touched with a position *beyond* the current `_reqCumulative` length? Can't — positions correspond to indexes within sorted.

Another scenario: the dirty suffix rebuild happens but `_reqDirtyFrom` is stale-large from an older cycle? It's reset each publish. Hmm.

Wait — bug: `_requestFactTouched` when `position == null` returns WITHOUT updating `_reqDirtyFrom` — fine since fact not in cache.

Let me think about the "existing" path more carefully, and the actual event order in the integration test. The flow might be replay via `appendAll` of persisted session then more live events, or `applyEvent`. Let me look at the test file.

Also there's a second suspicious path: `_markRequestCompleted`-ish code:

```dart
facts
  ..order = _rows.length.toDouble()
  ..status = status
  ..completedAt = message.timestamp
  ..usage = message.usage;
_requestFactTouched(facts);
```

Note `..order = _rows.length.toDouble()`. And `_requestFactTouched` checks `sorted[position + 1].order < fact.order` → resort. But hmm, there's a subtle bug: **the touched fact's order is updated BEFORE `_requestFactTouched` reads `sorted[position+1].order`**. That's intended.

But here's a REAL bug: `_requestFactTouched` triggers `_reqResort` only when the fact moves PAST its successor. But what if a touched fact's order update moves it past MULTIPLE successors... resort covers that.

OK let me think about the failure differently — cumulative = 200 means the fold for fact 4 seeded from null. When is `_reqCumulative[from-1]` null for from>0? `_reqCumulative` entries are non-null after folding facts with usage... wait — `_foldRequestNumber` stores `cumulative` which could be null if facts 1..from-1 all had null usage. Row 3 ('—') is a fact without usage. Rows 1,2 have usage. So `_reqCumulative[2]` should be 120 (after two usages).

Unless... `_reqCumulative` had LENGTH < 3 at that point? `_rebuildRequestsSuffix` seeds `cumulative = _reqCumulative[from - 1]` — if from-1 >= _reqCumulative.length → RangeError, not silent. So no.

Alternative: `_reqResort` path (`_rebuildAllRequests`) — that refolds everything from scratch; would give correct 400. Not it.

What about the **`_reqDirtyFrom` vs `_insertAddedRequests` ordering**: `_publishRequests` first calls `_insertAddedRequests()`, THEN computes `from = min(_reqDirtyFrom, _reqNumberRows.length)`. Note it compares `_reqDirtyFrom` against `_reqNumberRows.length` — the number ROWS length, not `_reqSorted.length`! If facts were added to sorted but number rows is shorter... from = min(dirtyFrom, numberRows.length). Then `_rebuildRequestsSuffix(from)` loops `for (i = from; i < sorted.length; i++)` and writes `_reqNumberRows[i]`. OK.

Hmm wait, here's a candidate bug: **fact touched whose position is beyond numberRows.length but within sorted.length**. Scenario: publish 1 with 2 facts (numberRows len 2, cumulative len 2, dirty reset). Fact 3 created → added list. Publish 2: insert added → sorted len 3; dirtyFrom untouched → from = min(1<<60, numberRows.len=2) = 2; suffix from 2 → folds fact 3, cumulative seeds `_reqCumulative[1]` = 120. Fine.

Now: publish 2 done with numberRows len 3. Fact 1 TOUCHED (e.g., re-finalized with new usage?). position 0 → dirtyFrom=0, no resort. Publish 3: no added; from = min(0, 3) = 0 → `_rebuildRequestsSuffix(0)` seeds null, refolds all 3. Correct.

Hmm. So where does 200 come from? Let me consider: **the fact usage is mutated AFTER folding but the cumulative was computed with the OLD usage, then a later publish only refolds a suffix**. E.g.:
- Publish A: fact 4 (turn 2/1) exists as a RUNNING fact (no usage) → folded with usage null → cumulative stays at 320? wait.

Sequence in a real session: `_requestStarted` creates fact with status running (usage null). Snapshot published (fact folded with null usage). Then completion sets …
